summary: Two-dimensional layout with token gaps: a fixed number of equal columns, or as many columns as fit for card and tile grids.
whenToUse: Card and tile grids: minItemWidth makes them responsive without breakpoints.
Dashboards and settings layouts with a fixed column count.
render={<ul />} when the cells are a list of items.
whenNotToUse: Tabular data with headers: use Table.
A single row or column: use Inline or Stack.

dos.title: Prefer minItemWidth for tiles
dos.text: Tiles reflow from four columns to one as space shrinks, with no media queries.

donts.title: Many fixed columns on small screens
donts.text: Twelve fixed columns at phone width make unreadable slivers. Use minItemWidth or fewer columns.

accessibility: A plain div by default with no role; it is not a data grid. Use Table for data.
Cells flow in DOM order, so reading and tab order follow the visual order row by row.
contentGuidelines: Not applicable: Grid holds no copy of its own.
